messages:
maria: Customer on eu-west reported repeated partial SSE responses then immediate reconnect loops. They see final event missing and then 502 on retry. Repro steps attached.

sasha: can you paste the minimal repro? thanks

maria: steps: 1) open SSE to /v1/streams with token X, 2) send prompt that produces a long stream (~8k tokens), 3) after ~40s client receives chunk then connection closes, client reconnects, sometimes receives truncated last event. curl repro:

maria: ```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \  
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \  
  'https://api.eu-west.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=fast-large'
```

james: logs from our edge for that session show repeated `write: broken pipe` and then `upstream read timeout`. ALB idle timeout is 60s. Client reported connection active via browser inspector, no TLS reneg.

ivorna: hmm: broken pipe implies client closed before we flushed final chunk. Could be browser-level preload or middlebox. Did the client use nginx/proxy in front of browser? any proxies?

maria: customer uses a mobile SDK which keeps socket open. They said it happens more on flaky networks. Also noticed token rotated mid-stream once.

sasha: token rotate mid-stream = likely auth middleware returned 401 on keepalive attempt? We should check if our streaming handler validates bearer per-chunk or relies on initial handshake only.

james: server does not re-validate token per event. But some infra components (auth sidecar) may reject long-lived requests if a session revokes. Log shows a 401 from auth-service ~39s in one trace followed by connection close.

ivorna: two axes: (A) network flakiness causing TCP resets -> client reconnects and we end up with partial output; (B) server-initiated close due to auth revocation. For keepalive, we send SSE comment pings every 15s. ALB idle 60s should be fine. But proxies sometimes drop if no non-comment bytes for L7 filters.

maria: customer suggested switching to binary ping events instead of comment pings. Any known differences?

sasha: comment pings (`: ping\n\n`) are lightweight and ignored by SSE parser but some proxies treat them as whitespace and drop. Using an actual `event: ping\ndata: {}` frame forces application bytes and can help.

james: opsbot run tcpdump? :opsbot:

opsbot: capturing 30s pcap for session id abcd1234 -> shows TCP RST from client after 42s and immediate reconnect. No server FIN.

ivorna: RST from client usually means client closed due to app logic (token expiry, SDK bug) or OS network stack. If token rotated -> client may intentionally reset.

maria: customer says mobile SDK reauth flow will close sockets when it refreshes token. That explains partial outputs if refresh happens mid-stream.

sasha: mitigation suggestions: 1) server should send periodic non-comment keepalive frames (e.g., `event: keepalive\ndata: {"t": <ts>}\n\n`) at interval < proxy idle. 2) recommend SDK keep token valid for duration or use token refresh handshake that does not close streams. 3) make server checkpoint emitted events so reconnect can resume with last_event_id header.

james: also worth adding server-side detection: if upstream auth rejects mid-stream, return JSON error event then close gracefully so clients don't interpret as partial data.

ivorna: can we patch streaming runtime to swap comment pings -> keepalive events behind a feature flag? I think yes, small change in generator loop.

maria: customer wants repro steps to show before/after. I'll ask them to test: set SDK to avoid token rotate mid-stream OR enable keepalive-event in our staging and retest.

sasha: ops follow-ups: - eng-infra to add feature flag + default to event pings for eu-west edge; - support to ask customer to reproduce with token stable and provide HAR; - SDK team to investigate refresh without RST.

maria: I'll log a ticket and share HAR + pcap. thanks :thumbsup:
